correctness.rationale: The scalar of a product of two fixed-trace unit quaternions is uniform on [cos(2theta),1], Haar has semicircle scalar density, and conjugation invariance makes scalar total variation exact. The two density-crossing regimes yield a piecewise elementary expression. Boundary inclusion is certified by max L^3(2-L)=27/16<pi^2/4; the derivative sign is the degree-eight P(L) whose derivative is strictly negative on [pi/2,2]. Endpoint signs prove a unique global root and precisely two symmetry-related optimal classes. Independent direct numerical quadrature and polynomial bisection were executed from verify.py. No inference from finite testing is used for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The first-step central class walk is singular to Haar; two steps are the first horizon with nontrivial TV error. The exact L1-optimal class angle for this natural compact-group harmonic convolution is non-equatorial, unique up to supplement, and subtly but provably different from the same family's L2 spectral optimum. This identifies the sharp finite-horizon invariant, a nontrivial threshold and an explicit polynomial optimizer.
